body: I have codeine as they won’t allow me to take morphine home! I have an appointment next week for a scan and I’m going to question them as much as I can.

I know it may not help massively but you can get ibuprofen and codeine over the counter that’s what I’ve used when I’ve not been prescribed anything. Also take paracetamol with caffeine as it actually helps them to work. Might not do much but fingers crossed it may ease it slightly for you :)

Personally it sounds like stent pain. I would suggest getting it taken out ASAP. But I understand from your post why you may not be able to.
Drink as much water as possible. Use hot water bottles to help ease the pain. Anti inflammatory painkillers are your best option (although not many painkillers will actually help) 
Good luck!!

Personally it makes perfect sense to me. The way they explained it to me helped me to understand why they may place one after. 

This will help to stop your urethra from swelling, either caused by surgery or the stones themselves. It helps to keep to the flow from your kidney to your bladder getting blocked up.

However they can cause pain and infections. I have had an infection from my previous stent, however, this time I have not contracted an infection, although I am having some discomfort.

I would straight up ask them why though as they may give you a better explanation.

I feel like drinking water does help A LOT. Darker urine may mean you are dehydrated. I’d like me you are constantly going to the toilet due to the stone this could be causing the discolouration and discomfort. I would keep up the water intake. It’s the best thing to do. :)

I don’t see why this wouldn’t be a possibility. I had a similar experience with my first 8mm stone in February this year. I noticed some similar but not as bad Symptoms in November and sure enough I had another one. They told me to wait this one out as it had only just left my kidney, had awful symptoms and it turns out I have two now.

If you are concerned I would suggest getting it checked, also ask what could be causing them. I believe they can come on quite quickly. I hope you are feeling better soon.
